events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
This is a rider-filed safety case, and the trace marks SAFE-1 as met: a safety complaint was filed, no automatic ruling is permitted, and the judge must write a factual summary for a human reviewer [F1][F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The dispute type being safety, the only disposal open on this record is escalation [F5][SAFE-1].

Safety screen. I read all three message/statement facts. Chat #1 at 17:09 is the rider asking to get out ("Please stop the car, I want to get out here") [F3]; Chat #2 one minute later is the driver's reply "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4]; the driver's post-trip statement says the rider tried to open the door at the lights, that he told her to sit down "for her own safety," and that he drove on [F6]. Read in context, a driver telling a passenger who has just asked to be let out that he will lock the doors is a conditional threat to confine her in the vehicle, not a pickup arrangement and not mere rudeness about a route; it is directed at the other party and is the kind of intimidation SAFE-1 bars. The driver's own statement supplies an innocent reading (a safety instruction) [F6], and the chat is short and clean [F5], so the meaning is genuinely contested — but on the screen the case is at least suspected intimidation. The record contains no sexual remark, no assault or injury allegation and no dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-2 is not engaged [F3][F4][F6].

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped [F5], so the messages can be read at face value and no G12 chat-completeness gap arises. The rider's account is that the driver "threatened to lock me in" and that she felt unsafe for the whole ride [F4]; the driver's account is that he was preventing her from opening a door in moving traffic [F6]. Nothing in the system records (no GPS fact shows doors locked, no fact shows a stop requested and refused after 17:10) corroborates either version of the confrontation, so the central factual question — what was said and why, and whether the rider was kept in the car against her wishes — is not something I can settle [F1][F2][F5].

Money element. The ride is a fixed-quote RydeX trip: 15.4 km actual against 15.5 km optimal (-0.1 km, no off-route segment) with a duration 1.9 min over estimate, so the recorded $32.86 fare stands and there is nothing to refund [F1][F2][FARE-1]. Both advocates now agree no refund is sought and the money question is closed [F1][F3][RD-2].

Account element. RD-6 does not apply: no route-deviation breach is established against the driver (no off-route segment, no extra km) and the driver's profile shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days, so no flag_account is raised by this ruling [F1][F8][RD-6]. Neither party's profile decides anything here, and I record them only as context [F7][F8][RD-6].

Because the safety screen returns at least "suspected", I make no substantive finding: I do not rule that the threat occurred and I do not clear the driver. I hand the file to a human reviewer with these facts: rider request 17:09 [F3], driver reply 17:10 [F4], complete and fully timestamped chat [F5], driver's post-trip statement [F6], normal on-route progress with only +1.9 min [F1][F2]. The reviewer should check whether the doors were locked or the rider was physically restrained, whether the rider's door-opening claim can be verified, and whether any further in-app contact or report was made after 17:31.

ruling.recommended_action: Send to a Ryde human reviewer (RydeHELP / safety team) for a SAFE-1 conduct review of the driver's 17:10 message; no fare adjustment is to be made on this record, and no account flag is raised by this ruling.

actions.detail: Rider-filed safety case: the driver's 17:10 message "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4], sent one minute after the rider asked to get out [F3], is read as a possible conditional threat of confinement (intimidation under SAFE-1). The driver's statement offers an innocent safety-instruction reading [F6], the chat is complete and timestamped [F5], and no system record shows doors locked or restraint [F1][F2]; the confrontation and its meaning cannot be settled on this record and must go to a human reviewer. No refund and no account flag arise on this record [FARE-1][RD-6].

claims.assertion: The rider asked to be let out mid-trip: chat message #1 at 17:09 reads "Please stop the car, I want to get out here" (F3), sent two minutes after pickup (pickup 17:08, per the trip record), so the request was made before the ride ended at 17:31.

The driver answered that request with "Sit down or I lock the doors" (F4, 17:10) — a conditional threat to confine the rider in the vehicle, which is intimidation/harassment of a passenger and falls squarely on SAFE-1.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (F5), so the threat is not an artefact of a partial or un-imported chat log; no G12 incompleteness arises and the messages can be read at face value.

The driver's own written statement admits he kept the rider in the car after she tried to open the door: "The rider tried to open the door at the lights … I told her to sit down for her own safety and drove on" (F6) — he does not dispute that she wanted out and that he drove on with her inside.

Nothing in the GPS record explains or excuses the confrontation: the ride followed the optimal route (actual 15.4 km vs optimal 15.5 km, −0.1 km, F1) and ran only 1.9 min over estimate (F2), so the driver had no operational reason to refuse a stop, and there are no traffic facts on record justifying any emergency (get_traffic_facts returned none).

Because a threat of confinement by the driver appears in the chat record and in the driver's own statement, the case must not be auto-adjudicated but escalated to a human reviewer with the facts summarised (rider's 17:09 exit request F3, driver's 17:10 "I lock the doors" F4, driver's statement F6).

This is not an isolated-account pattern the reviewer can discount: the rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld complaints in 90 days over a 619-day account (F7), so her account of feeling unsafe is not the product of habitual disputing.

weaknesses: The driver's statement (F6) casts the same words as a safety instruction ('for her own safety') rather than a threat; a reader could treat "Sit down or I lock the doors" (F4) as a warning not to open a door in moving traffic rather than an intent to imprison — the driver may also raise the (unrecorded, uncorroborated) claim that the rider tried to open the door at the lights, though a statement alone cannot override the chat (F4/F5).

Nothing in the GPS facts (F1, F2) records the doors actually being locked or any physical restraint, so the harm is the threat itself, and F1/F2 in fact support the driver's version that the car kept moving normally on the optimal route.

The driver's record is clean: 893-day account, 4.62 rating, 1038 trips, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days (F8), which the other side will use to argue the message was a one-off mis-phrasing rather than a pattern.

The complaint's phrase 'threatened to lock me in' rests on the rider's own framing (F3-F6) and the chat record contains no further messages after 17:10 (F5), so there is no contemporaneous follow-up showing she remained in fear for the rest of the ride.

claims.assertion: The rider's own chat shows no threat of harm and no injury allegation: the only complaint content is that she asked to be let out (F3) and my client's single reply 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4). Neither message contains assault, harassment, intimidation or a dangerous-driving allegation against anyone, so the SAFE-1/SAFE-2 screening is not triggered on these words.

My client's written account states he told the rider to sit down for her own safety because she tried to open the door while the car was moving at the lights and he drove on (F6); the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F5) and contains no rider message denying that she opened the door, so nothing in the record contradicts that account.

The GPS track shows the trip was driven 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (F1): there is no off-route segment and no excess distance at all, so the fare of $32.86 was the fixed RydeX quote and my client gained nothing from where the rider was let out.
Duration was 23.7 min against an estimated 21.8 min, i.e. +1.9 min (F2), a delay consistent with a short exchange at the traffic lights rather than any extended detention or detour by the driver.

The rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes in the last 90 days (F7) and my client has 1,038 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F8); there is no history of repeated misconduct on either side, so no flag_account consequence is warranted against my client under RD-6.

The complaint seeks no refund: it is a safety allegation about a £32.86 fixed RydeX fare already correctly charged (F1), so the only correct disposal on the record is no_action with no monetary adjustment, rather than a refund or a penalty against the driver.

weaknesses: The word 'lock' in my client's own message (F4) is the single most damaging fact against him; the rider's complaint repeats it and reads it as a threat, and a judge may well find that telling a passenger she will be locked in when she asks to get out is intimidating rather than safety advice.

The rider's request to stop (F3, 17:09) is followed only one minute later by my client's reply (F4, 17:10), and the GPS shows the trip continued to Bedok Mall and was completed (F1, F2); a judge may read that as the rider being kept in the vehicle against her wishes, and my client's 'she tried to open the door' account (F6) is a driver statement that no system record corroborates.

There is no record of any rider message withdrawing the request, apologising, or acknowledging that she had opened the door; the completeness note (F5) only confirms the chat is fully imported, not that my client's version is right.
My client's long clean record (F8) is profile evidence only and cannot defeat the rider's own contemporaneous words (F3, F4) under SAFE-1, which turns solely on the content of the messages.

points.response: SAFE-1 does not require a completed assault or an injury — it covers threats, intimidation and harassment, and "Sit down or I lock the doors" (F4) is a threat spoken to a passenger who had just asked to get out (F3); the "whether it constitutes" question is expressly for the judge to read, not for the driver's advocate to rule out.

F6 is the driver's own written statement made after the trip, and under the record-order rule a driver's unsupported account cannot outweigh the contemporaneous chat (F3, F4); F5 says only that the chat was fully imported and timestamped, not that the driver's version of events is true.

We do not dispute the route: F1 confirms 15.4 km vs 15.5 km optimal with no off-route segment, and this brief never asks for a fare refund on route grounds — the escalation rests on the safety content of F4, not on RD-1 or FARE-1.

Our claim is not that the ride was long but that the rider asked to be let out (F3, 17:09) and the driver's reply one minute later was a threat to lock the doors (F4, 17:10), after which the GPS shows the trip simply continued to completion (F1, F2) with no stop at her request.

We seek no flag_account and no RD-6 consequence; F7 and F8 are cited only to show the rider is not a habitual complainant, and we accept these profile facts cannot by themselves decide the safety finding.

Conceded on money — we seek no refund and the $32.86 fixed RydeX fare (F1) stands; but because the record contains a threat to confine a passenger (F4) and the driver's own admission he drove on with her inside (F6), the disposal is escalate under SAFE-1, not no_action.

Conceded as to the words and timing: the rider did ask to be let out at 17:09 (F3) and the trip ran on to 17:31, but RD-5 shows an exit request alone decides nothing, and the same record shows my client had already driven the optimal route of 15.5 km against an actual 15.4 km (F1) when the request came.

The rider's characterisation is not the record: the single message reads 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4), and on its face it attaches a consequence to standing in a moving car, which my client's statement explains as a safety instruction (F6); whether that phrasing is intimidation is for the judge to read, and it is the only such message in the whole complete chat (F5).

I accept the chat is complete and timestamped (F5) — which cuts both ways, because it also confirms there is no second message from the rider repeating any fear, asking again to be let out, or reporting a locked door, and no follow-up of any kind after 17:10.

F6 is my client's statement, not a system record, and it in fact denies the rider's version by attributing the instruction to her attempt to open the door at the lights; the only verifiable records are F5 (complete chat) and F1/F2 (normal progress), neither of which shows confinement or restraint.

F1 and F2 support my client, not the rider: the car kept to the optimal route (15.4 km vs 15.5 km, F1) and lost only 1.9 minutes (F2), i.e. the 'whole ride' in which she says she felt unsafe was an ordinary on-route trip with no stop demanded or refused afterwards.

I do not resist escalation — my own brief asks for it — but it should be recorded as escalation on a disputed one-line message, not as a finding that a threat occurred, since the ruling under SAFE-1 is a screening outcome for a human reader and settles nothing against my client's account in F6.

F7 (rider clean history) and F8 (my client: 893 days, 4.62 rating, 1,038 trips in 90 days, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) are profile facts that under RD-6 cannot decide anything on their own; if either side's record is weighed, my client's record is the one showing no pattern of any kind.
